title: Inflation and the 2% target
summary: The Bank of England's inflation target page provides current status: Bank Rate at 3.75% (next decision due 30 April 2026) and CPI inflation at 3.3%, above the 2% target. The page explains the inflation targeting framework and the requirement for the Governor to write to the Chancellor if inflation deviates more than 1 percentage point from target. This is an informational/educational page rather than a specific policy event or data release.
key_points: Current Bank Rate: 3.75% (next monetary policy meeting: 30 April 2026)
Current CPI inflation: 3.3%, above the 2% target by 1.3 percentage points
CPI is measured by the ONS collecting approximately 180,000 prices for about 700 items monthly
If inflation deviates more than 1 percentage point from target (below 1% or above 3%), the Governor must explain to the Chancellor in writing
Recent inflation letters sent: December 2025, September 2025, June 2025, March 2024
The inflation targeting framework is designed to help businesses set prices and people plan spending
why_it_matters: This page is background reference material explaining the Bank of England's inflation mandate and current status. It is not a catalyst but rather provides foundational context for understanding BoE monetary policy.
